summary: Unexpected 429s during mixed embedding + chat priority split after regional failover
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DataBridge AI reports repeated 429 throttles after a cross-region failover that occurred 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC. Traffic pattern is hybrid: short-lived chat sessions (low token, high QPS) and batched embedding uploads (bursty token usage). They observe 429s primarily on embedding endpoints but also see degraded success for chat requests during the same window.

Impact:
- Customer reports 15% request failure rate for embed jobs and increased retry traffic causing cascading load.
- Affects their nightly ingestion pipelines and real-time chat features; revenue-impacting for customer (billing tied to late SLAs).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id db-ai-dedicated-12
- Region: primary us-east-1 with geo-failover to us-west-2 triggered at 2026-03-11T02:10:22Z by automated healthcheck.
- API surface: /v1/embeddings (batched multipart), /v1/chat/stream (short sessions).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Trigger a geo-failover by simulating degraded origin (they executed a canary kill).
2) Run ingestion job with 600 concurrent workers producing 10–20 embed requests each (payloads ~512 tokens).
3) Simultaneously start 300 concurrent chat sessions with average 3 token responses.
4) Observe 429s within 30s of failover and elevated retry waves for ~12 minutes.

Customer-provided logs and timestamps attached in comments.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: quota accounting skew between per-route and tenant windows after failover. Observed token-window refill drift on edge proxies (token-buckets not synchronized during NAT/IP change). Secondary hypothesis: healthcheck traffic from origin incrementing tenant counters on new edge causing preemption of burst credits.

What we checked so far:
- Datadog dashboards: spike on rate_limiter.count 2026-03-11T02:10:40Z matching their failover timestamp.
- Token-bucket metrics: origin refill timestamp gap ~18s during NAT remap.
- Edge logs: multiple ephemeral API keys reused through a pooled proxy; connection reuse observed in ingress logs.
- Autoscaler: dedicated pool scaled +2 instances ~4 minutes after failover; warmup traffic likely contributed to quota exhaustion.

Preliminary findings:
- Per-route burst bucket was set low for embedding route on this dedicated pool (configured to conserve burst for chat). During failover, queued embedding workers pushed through queued traffic that consumed tenant-level burst and starved per-route allocations.
- Healthcheck and warmup probes appeared to be counted against tenant-level tokens; combined with multiple ephemeral connections this amplified refill skew.

Related signals and dashboards:
- Datadog dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/rlq-123/rate-limiter-overview
- Tracing: span ids in logs correspond to ingress host 10.3.7.19 which shows NAT IP churn.

customer_reproduction_steps: Customer reproduced by: 1) running a synthetic failover at 02:10 UTC, 2) starting ingestion with 600 parallel workers (8s stagger), 3) launching 300 chat sessions at same time. They captured Datadog spans and provided request IDs in comment #1.
support_actions:
Actions taken by Support so far:
- Scoped logs and confirmed tenant-level 0-token events at failover.
- Increased per-route burst temporarily for DataBridge AI on embedding route for 90 minutes to relieve immediate pressure.
- Instructed customer to stagger embed workers and to add jitter to retries.
- Eng paged to investigate token-bucket refills and edge NAT handling (see linked PR).
resolution:
Mitigation applied: temporary per-route burst raise for /v1/embeddings and rate-limiter config change to avoid counting healthcheck/warmup probes against tenant burst during failover. Engineering change merged (infra PR #4123) that: 1) marks internal healthcheck probe traffic as exempt from tenant burst accounting during a known failover window, and 2) synchronizes bucket refill time across edge nodes on NAT remap.

Follow-ups & next steps:
- Follow-up task to update runbook: add explicit guidance to hold large embedding batch windows during geo-failovers. (Owner: SRE Playbooks).
- Schedule a dedicated-pool config audit for per-route burst baselines for large ingestion customers. (Due: 2026-03-20).
- Customer agreed to adopt staggered worker pattern and enable built-in retry-jitter in their ingestion orchestrator.
